167.subject: Botany
167.text: Which of the following is responsible for the mechanical support, protein synthesis and enzyme transport?
167.sol: Endoplasmic reticulum functions as cytoskeleton or intracellular and ultrastructural skeletal framework by providing mechanical support to colloidal cytoplasmic matrix. Proteins and enzymes synthesized by ribosomes enter the channels of rough endoplasmic reticulum both for intracellular use as well as extracellular transport.

192.subject: Botany
192.text: Which of these are most widely used in genetic engineering?
192.sol: Plastids are semiautonomous cell organelles. They take part in storage and synthesis of organic compounds. Mitochondria are called the power houses of the cell as they are the centres of Kreb's cycle of respiration liberating the maximum amount of energy. Ribosomes are submicroscopic cell organelles manufacturing protein. Plasmids are defined as autonomous elements, whose genomes exist in the cell as the extrachromosomal unit. These are the chromosomal elements found in bacteria. Plasmids are used as cloning vector

342.subject: Botany
342.text: Select one of the following pairs of important features distinguishing Gnetum from Cycas and Pinus and showing affinities with angiosperms.
options: Absence of resin duct and leaf venation
Presence of vessel elements and absence of archegonia
342.sol: Unlike Cycas and Pinus, Gnetum shows the occurrence of vessel elements and the absence of archegonia. Archegonia are altogether absent in the female gametophyte and vessels occur in the xylem along with the tracheids in the secondary wood. Thus Gnetum shows affinities with angiosperms. Besides it resembles angiosperms in several other aspects like presence of tetrasporic embryo sac, free nuclear divisions in the embryo sac, two cotyledonous embryo etc.

2052.text: It is a disease which mainly affects mucous membrane of urinogenital tract. In males, burning feeling on passing urine, after a yellow discharge occurs, that is accompanied by fever, headache and feeling of illness. Its name is
2052.sol: Gonorrhoea is caused by a bacterium, Neisseria gonorrhoeae. It spreads through sexual contact, common toilets and underclothes. Gonorrhoea affects both male and female genitals. 71742.subject: Chemistry
71742.text: Which of the following is always a bidentate ligand?
71742.sol: Ammonia ( NH₃ ), water ( H₂O ), and carbon monoxide ( CO ) are monodentate ligands because they donate only one pair of electrons to the central metal atom or ion. Ethylenediamine ( H₂N-CH₂-CH₂-NH₂ ) is a bidentate ligand because it has two nitrogen atoms, each with a lone pair of electrons, which can simultaneously coordinate to the central metal atom or ion. Answer: Ethylenediamine

71957.subject: Chemistry
71957.text: What type of solid is the diamond?
71957.sol: Diamond is an allotrope of carbon in which each carbon atom is bonded to four other carbon atoms via strong covalent bonds in a tetrahedral geometry. This continuous three-dimensional arrangement of covalent bonds forms a giant network structure. Therefore, diamond is classified as a covalent network solid. Answer: Covalent network solid

72122.subject: Physics
72122.text: A parallel plate capacitor filled with oil of dielectric constant 3 between the plates, has a capacitance 'C'. If the oil is completely removed, then the capacitance of the capacitor will be
72122.sol: The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor filled with a dielectric of constant K is given by C = K ₀ A d . Given K = 3 , the initial capacitance is C = 3 ₀ A d . When the oil is completely removed, the medium between the plates becomes air or vacuum, for which the dielectric constant is 1 . The new capacitance becomes C' = ₀ A d . From the initial equation, we have ₀ A d = C 3 . Therefore, the new capacitance is C' = C 3 . Answer: C 3

72478.subject: Physics
72478.text: The speed of the transverse wave on the stretched string under tension T₁ is v₁ . If the tension in the string is increased by T₁ , the speed of the transverse wave is v₂ . If is the linear density of the string, then v₂ = xv₁ . The value of x is
72478.sol: The speed of a transverse wave on a stretched string is given by v = T , where T is the tension and is the linear mass density. For the initial state, the tension is T₁ , so the speed is: v₁ = T₁ The tension is increased by T₁ , so the new tension is T₂ = T₁ + T₁ = 2T₁ . The new speed is: v₂ = 2T₁ = 2 T₁ = 2 v₁ Comparing this with v₂ = x v₁ , we get x = 2 . Answer: 2

79388.subject: Botany
79388.sol: In dicot stems, cambium is present between phloem and xylem. 84550.subject: Zoology
84550.text: Which one of the following techniques is safest for the detection of cancer?
84550.sol: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) is a non-invasive technique, which uses strong magnetic field and provides information about chemistry, metabolic and biochemical data of tissue without time consuming chemical analysis. It is the safest technique for the detection of cancer since it does not utilize radiations and therefore, does not cause any side effect. Histopathological study is not safe as it is invasive technique while radiography and Computed Tomography (CT) use harmful X -rays.

84696.subject: Zoology

A growing ovarian follicle gradually secretes increasing amounts of estrogen. This, in turn, leads to a sudden surge of LH secretion by the pituitary. 115962.sol: The paragraph states that among the oxoacids formed by nitrogen, HNO 3 (nitric acid) is the most important.

116098.subject: Chemistry
116098.text: Which xenon fluoride has a distorted octahedral structure in the gas phase?
116098.sol: XeF 6 has a distorted octahedral structure in the gas phase due to its seven electron pairs (6 bonding pairs and one lone pair).

options: The acidic character is not mentioned
116155.sol: The paragraph states that the acidic character of these hydrides increases from H 2 O to H 2 Te.

Chloride ions have a weak positive charge.
Chloride ions have a strong negative charge.
Chloride ions have a weak negative charge.

116486.text: What is the stability of half-filled d subshell (d5) in Mn2+ related to?
116486.sol: The stability of half-filled d subshell (d5) in Mn2+ is related to the highest negative enthalpy of hydration.

116703.subject: Chemistry
116703.text: Which types of acids react with Cu by being reduced?
116703.sol: Only oxidizing acids (nitric and hot concentrated sulfuric) react with Cu, with the acids being reduced.

119506.text: What role does aluminum chloride (Lewis acid) play in the reaction of aromatic carboxylic acids with Friedel-Crafts reagents?
119506.sol: Aluminum chloride (Lewis acid) bonds to the carboxyl group in the reaction of aromatic carboxylic acids with Friedel-Crafts reagents.

119539.subject: Chemistry
119539.text: Assertion: Benzoic acid does not undergo Freidel Crafts reaction. Reason: The carboxyl group in benzoic acid donates electrons into the ring through resonance.
options: Both assertion and reason are correct statements, and reason is the correct explanation of the assertion.
Both assertion and reason are correct statements, but reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion.
Assertion is correct, but reason is wrong statement.
Assertion is wrong, but reason is correct statement.
119539.sol: Why: - Benzoic acid doesn't undergo Friedel-Crafts (alkylation/acylation) because the -COOH group is strongly deactivating: it withdraws electrons by -M (resonance) and -I (inductive) effects and also complexes with ( AlCl ₃ ), killing the ring's reactivity. - The reason given is false:-COOH does not donate electrons into the ring; it withdraws them.

119619.subject: Chemistry
119619.text: What is the characteristic odour of the products formed in the Carbylamine reaction?
119619.sol: The products formed in the Carbylamine reaction, isocyanides or carbylamines, are foul-smelling substances.

119898.sol: Coupling of diazonium chloride with phenols occurs in basic medium and p -hydroxyazobenzene is formed. Coupling of diazonium chlorine with aniline occurs in acidic medium only.

If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.

Instead, the other benzene ring gets oxidised giving o -nitrophthalic acid as shown below :

120455.subject: Chemistry
120455.text: How does the branching of hydrocarbon chain of synthetic detergents affect their biodegradability?
options: Branching of the hydrocarbon chain increases biodegradability.
Biodegradability depends on other factors unrelated to branching.
Branching of the hydrocarbon chain has no effect on biodegradability.
Less branching leads to easy biodegradability.
120455.sol: Correct Option is : (D) Less branching leads to easy biodegradability.

Acetylation of glucose with acetic anhydride gives glucose pentaacetate which confirms the presence of five –O
On prolonged heating with HI, it forms n-hexane
On oxidation with nitric acid, glucose as well as gluconic acid both yield a dicarboxylic acid, saccharic acid
120949.sol: Correct Option is : (A) The pentaacetate of glucose does not react with hydroxylamine indicating the absence of a free CHO group.

120986.subject: Chemistry
120986.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I List-II (A) Apoenzyme (I) Transiently bound organic compound (B) Prosthetic group (II) Protein portion of enzyme (C) Co-enzyme (III) Forms coordination bonds (D) Metal ion (IV) Tightly bound organic compound Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
120986.sol: The protein portion of the enzyme is called the apoenzyme. Prosthetic groups are organic compounds that are tightly bound to the apoenzyme. Co-enzymes are organic compounds whose association with the apoenzyme is only transient, usually occurring during the course of catalysis. Metal ions form coordination bonds with side chains at the active site and at the same time form one or more coordination bonds with the substrate. Therefore, the correct match is (A)-(II), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(III). Answer: (A)-(II), (B)

121125.subject: Botany
121125.text: Which process involves grouping anything into convenient categories based on observable characteristics?
121125.sol: Name of the author appears after the specific epithet, i.e., at the end of the biological name and is written in an abbreviated form, e.g., Mangifera indica Linn. It indicates that this species was first described by Linnaeus. Since it is nearly impossible to study all the living organisms, it is necessary to devise some means to make this possible. This process is classification. Classification is the process by which anything is grouped into convenient categories based on some easily observable characters. For ex

121743.subject: Botany
121743.text: Where can the union of gametes take place in oogamous species of brown algae?
options: In water or within the oogonium
On the surface of the water
121743.sol: The algae reproduce by vegetative, asexual and sexual methods. Vegetative reproduction is by fragmentation. Each fragment develops into a thallus. Asexual reproduction is by the production of different types of spores, the most common being the zoospores. They are flagellated (motile) and on germination gives rise to new plants. Sexual reproduction takes place through fusion of two gametes. These gametes can be flagellated and similar in size (as in Ulothrix) or non-flagellated (non-motile) but similar in size (as

121808.subject: Botany
121808.text: What are Pteridophytes commonly used for?
121808.sol: The Pteridophytes include horsetails and ferns. Pteridophytes are used for medicinal purposes and as soil-binders . They are also frequently grown as ornamentals. Evolutionarily, they are the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues – xylem and phloem. The pteridophytes are found in cool, damp, shady places though some may flourish well in sandy-soil conditions. In pteridophytes, the main plant body is a sporophyte which is differentiated into true root, stem and leaves (Figure 3.3). These organs posses

121814.subject: Botany
121814.text: What structures do some Pteridophytes' sporophylls form?
121814.sol: The Pteridophytes include horsetails and ferns. Pteridophytes are used for medicinal purposes and as soil-binders. They are also frequently grown as ornamentals. Evolutionarily, they are the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues – xylem and phloem. The pteridophytes are found in cool, damp, shady places though some may flourish well in sandy-soil conditions. In pteridophytes, the main plant body is a sporophyte which is differentiated into true root, stem and leaves (Figure 3.3). These organs possess

122062.subject: Botany
122062.text: Mannitol is the stored food in of
122062.sol: Fucus belongs to class-Phaeophyceae, in which reserve food is found in form of laminarin, mannitol and oil. Chara belongs to class-Chlorophyceae, in which reserve food is found in form of starch and oil. Porphyra and Gracillaria belong to class-Rhodophyceae, in which reserve food is found in form of floridean starch and Galactan- SO ₄ polymers.

122230.subject: Botany
122230.text: What is the second largest animal phylum?
122230.sol: Molluscs are the second largest animal phylum. Molluscs are terrestrial or aquatic (marine or fresh water) having an organ-system level of organisation. They are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic and coelomate animals.Body is covered by a calcareous shell and is unsegmented with a distinct head,muscular foot and visceral hump in Molluscs. The space between the hump and the mantle is called the mantle cavity in which feather like gills are present. They have respiratory and excretory functions. The anterior hea

122734.subject: Botany
options: A flower with both stamens and pistils
A flower with no reproductive organs
122734.sol: The flower is the reproductive unit in the angiosperms. It is meant for sexual reproduction. A typical flower has four different kinds of whorls arranged successively on the swollen end of the stalk or pedicel, called thalamus or receptacle. These are calyx, corolla, androecium and gynoecium. Calyx and corolla are accessory organs, while androecium and gynoecium are reproductive organs. In some flowers like lily, the calyx and corolla are not distinct and are termed as perianth. When a flower has both androecium an

123310.subject: Botany
123310.text: Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option: 1. Palisade parenchyma are oval, round and loosely attached 2. Spongy parechyma are elongated cells that are arranged vertically 3. In dicots The abaxial epidermis generally bears more stomata than the adaxial epidermis. 4. The lamina shows three main parts, namely, epidermis, mesophyll and vascular system
123310.sol: The adaxially placed palisade parenchyma is made up of elongated cells, which are arranged vertically and parallel to each other. The oval or round and loosely arranged spongy parenchyma is situated below the palisade cells and extends to the lower epidermis.

123389.subject: Botany
123389.text: Terms Structures A. Cuticle 1. Outermost protective layer covering the epidermis B. Trichomes 2. Hair-like structures on the epidermis C. Stomata 3. Parenchymatous cells between vascular bundles D. Medullary Rays 4. Pores in the epidermis for gas exchange
123389.sol: The cuticle is the protective layer on the epidermis, trichomes are hair-like structures, stomata are pores for gas exchange, and medullary rays are parenchymatous cells between vascular bundles.

123529.subject: Botany
123529.text: What is the importance of DNA replication during cell division?
options: To ensure correct formation of progeny cells
To copy the genetic information of the cell
123529.sol: Cell division is a very important process in all living organisms. During the division of a cell, DNA replication and cell growth also take place. All these processes, i.e., cell division, DNA replication, and cell growth, hence, have to take place in a coordinated way to ensure correct division and formation of progeny cells containing intact genomes. The sequence of events by which a cell duplicates its genome, synthesises the other constituents of the cell and eventually divides into two daughter cells is termed

123691.subject: Botany
123691.text: What is the significance of diakinesis stage?
options: It represents transition to prophase II
123691.sol: The final stage of meiotic prophase I is diakinesis. This is marked by terminalisation of chiasmata. : During this phase the chromosomes are fully condensed and the meiotic spindle is assembled to prepare the homologous chromosomes for separation. By the end of diakinesis, the nucleolus disappears and the nuclear envelope also breaks down. Diakinesis represents transition to metaphase By the end of diakinesis, the nucleolus disappears and the nuclear envelope also breaks down. Diakinesis represents transition to me

123744.subject: Botany
123744.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: During Leptotene, chromosomes start pairing together and this process of association is called synapsis. Reason: The complex formed by a pair of synapsed homologous chromosomes is called a monovalent.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
123744.sol: During Zygotene stage, chromosomes start pairing together and this process of association is called synapsis. The complex formed by a pair of synapsed homologous chromosomes is called a bivalent or tetrad.

123919.subject: Botany
123919.text: Microtubule depolymerizing drug such as colchicine is expected to
options: induce formation of multiple contractile rings.
123919.sol: Colchicine is an alkaloid derived from the autumn crocus, Colchicum autumnale. It inhibits spindle formation in cells during mitosis so that chromosomes cannot separate during anaphase, thus inducing multiple sets of chromosomes. It does not affect cytokinesis.

124160.subject: Botany
124160.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Mitochondria are the sites of anerobic respiration Reason: They produce energy in the form of lactic acid
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion are Reason are false
124160.sol: Mitochondria are the sites of aerobic respiration. They produce cellular energy in the form of ATP, hence they are called ‘power houses’ of the cell.

124291.subject: Botany
124291.text: Match List-I with List-II regarding the structural features of cell organelles. List-I List-II (A) Matrix (I) Infoldings in mitochondria (B) Cristae (II) Space enclosed by inner membrane of chloroplast (C) Stroma (III) Dense homogeneous substance in inner compartment of mitochondria (D) Thylakoids (IV) Flattened membranous sacs in stroma Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
124291.sol: The mitochondrion and chloroplast are double membrane-bound organelles. The inner compartment of the mitochondrion is filled with a dense homogeneous substance called the matrix. The inner mitochondrial membrane forms a number of infoldings called the cristae towards the matrix. The space limited by the inner membrane of the chloroplast is called the stroma. A number of organised flattened membranous sacs called the thylakoids are present in the stroma. Thus, the correct match is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(

124346.subject: Botany
124346.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Theodore Schwann concluded that the presence of a cell wall is a unique character of plant cells. Reason (R): He examined a large number of plants and observed that all plants are composed of different kinds of cells which form the tissues of the plant. In the light of the above statements, choose
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but Reason is false
Assertion is false but Reason is true
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
124346.sol: According to NCERT, Theodore Schwann (1839), a British Zoologist, studied different types of animal cells and reported that cells had a thin outer layer which is today known as the plasma membrane. He also concluded, based on his studies on plant tissues, that the presence of a cell wall is a unique character of plant cells. Thus, the Assertion (A) is true. The Reason (R) describes the work of Matthias Schleiden (1838), a German Botanist, who examined a large number of plants and observed that all plants are compos

124612.subject: Botany
124612.text: Which is the correct statement about the zones that have elongated the most in the given figure?
options: Only Zone A and B have elongated the most.
Zones that have elongated the most are immediately behind the base
Zones that have elongated the most are immediately behind the apex.

124750.subject: Botany

List-I List-II (A) Charles Darwin and Francis Darwin (I) Avena coleoptile (B) F.W. Went (II) Internodal segments of tobacco stem (C) E. Kurosawa (III) Coleoptiles of canary grass (D) F. Skoog and co-workers (IV) Uninfected rice seedlings Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

Went isolated auxin from the tips of coleoptiles of oat (Avena) seedlings. E. 124902.subject: Botany
124902.text: Which one of the following doesn't help in molecule transport?
124902.sol: Surface tension doesn't help in molecule transport. The process of diffusion and osmosis transport molecules is without using energy but in case of active transport energy (ATP) is used.

125019.subject: Botany
125019.text: What happens to glucose in aerobic respiration that does not happen in fermentation?
options: It is converted to pyruvic acid
It is completely degraded to CO2 and H2O
It produces only two ATP molecules
125019.sol: • Fermentation accounts for only a partial breakdown of glucose whereas in aerobic respiration it is completely degraded to CO2 and H2O . • In fermentation there is a net gain of only two molecules of ATP for each molecule of glucose degraded to pyruvic acid whereas many more molecules of ATP are generated under aerobic conditions. • NADH is oxidized to NAD+ rather slowly in fermentation, however the reaction is very vigorous in case of aerobic respiration

125295.subject: Botany
125295.text: What is the ultimate source of energy for all living forms on earth?
125295.sol: All animals including human beings depend on plants for their food. Have you ever wondered from where plants get their food? Green plants, in fact, have to make or rather synthesise the food they need and all other organisms depend on them for their needs.The green plants make or rather synthesise the food they need through photosynthesis and are therefore called autotrophs. The autotrophic nutrition is found only in plants and all other organisms that depend on the green plants for food are heterotrophs. Green pla

125586.subject: Botany
125586.text: Components of Calvin Cycle Requirements or Functions A. CO2 1. Molecule that enters the Calvin cycle and requires energy for fixation. B. ATP 2. Required in the Calvin cycle; 3 molecules are needed per CO2 molecule fixed. C. NADPH 3. A process that produces additional ATP to balance the ATP and NADPH requirements. D. Cyclic Phosphorylation 4. Required in the Calvin cycle; 2 molecules are needed per CO2 molecule fixed
125586.sol: A - 1: CO2 is the molecule that enters the Calvin cycle and requires energy (ATP and NADPH) for fixation. B - 2: ATP is required in the Calvin cycle, with 3 molecules needed for every CO2 molecule fixed. C - 4: NADPH is also required in the Calvin cycle, with 2 molecules needed per CO2 molecule fixed. D - 3: Cyclic phosphorylation produces additional ATP to balance the difference in the number of ATP and NADPH required in the Calvin cycle.

125661.subject: Botany
125661.text: Read the following statement regarding the first step of the Calvin cycle and select the option that correctly fills the blanks (X), (Y), and (Z). In the Calvin cycle, the enzyme (X) catalyzes the addition of C O₂ to a (Y)-carbon acceptor molecule, resulting in the formation of two molecules of a (Z)-carbon compound.
125661.sol: The first step of the Calvin cycle is carboxylation. During this step, the enzyme RuBisCO (Ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase-oxygenase) catalyzes the addition of CO₂ to Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate (RuBP). RuBP is a 5-carbon (5C) acceptor molecule. This reaction results in an unstable 6-carbon intermediate that immediately splits into two molecules of 3-phosphoglyceric acid (3-PGA), which is a 3-carbon (3C) compound. Thus, (X) is RuBisCO, (Y) is 5, and (Z) is 3. Selecting PEP carboxylase, 3, and 4 incorrectly describe

125715.subject: Botany
125715.text: Which one of the following categories of organisms do not evolve oxygen during photosynthesis?
options: C ₄ plants with Kranz anatomy
125715.sol: The photosynthetic bacteria (e.g. purple non-sulphur bacteria) photosynthesise using bacteriochlorophylls a and b in anoxic environments, such as the bottom mud of ponds and other stagnant water, although they are able to survive in air. The reducing agent involved is hydrogen rather than water, so oxygen is not produced. These bacteria efficiently use infrared light for photosynthesis.

126156.subject: Botany
126156.text: Parts of ovule Location/Features A. Hilum 1. Mass of cell surrounding the embryo sac B. Nucellus 2. Basal part C. Chalaza 3. Two envelopes surrounding the ovule D. Integuments 4. Region of ovule where funicle is attached
126156.sol: The ovule is a small structure attached to the placenta by means of a stalk called funicle. The body of the ovule fuses with funicle in the region called hilum. Thus, hilum represents the junction between ovule and funicle. Each ovule has one or two protective envelopes called integuments. Integuments encircle the nucellus except at the tip where a small opening called the micropyle is organised. Opposite the micropylar end, is the chalaza, representing the basal part of the ovule. Enclosed within the integuments i

126180.subject: Botany
126180.text: A genetically controlled mechanism in which pollen grains of a flower are unable to grow completely on the stigma of the same flower is called ___.
126180.sol: A genetically controlled mechanism in which pollen grains of a flower are unable to grow completely on the stigma of the same flower is called Self-incompatibility

127200.subject: Botany
127200.text: What is the main reason behind Steller's sea cow and passenger pigeon extinction?
127200.sol: : Humans have always depended on nature for food and shelter, but when ‘need’ turns to ‘greed’, it leads to over -exploitation of natural resources. Many species extinctions in the last 500 years (Steller’s sea cow, passenger pigeon) were due to overexploitation by humans. Presently many marine fish populations around the world are over harvested, endangering the continued existence of some commercially important species

127399.subject: Botany
127399.text: Which of the following statements regarding biodiversity conservation is incorrect?
options: In-situ conservation involves protecting the entire ecosystem to protect the threatened species.
Seed banks allow the preservation of seeds of different genetic strains of commercially important plants for l
National parks and wildlife sanctuaries are established for ex-situ conservation of biodiversity.
Sacred groves in Meghalaya are the last refuges for a large number of rare and threatened plants.
127399.sol: National parks and wildlife sanctuaries are examples of in-situ (on-site) conservation, where threatened species are protected within their natural habitat along with the entire ecosystem. Ex-situ conservation involves taking the species out of their natural habitat into special settings like zoological parks, botanical gardens, and wildlife safari parks. The other statements are correct as per NCERT: in-situ conservation protects the whole ecosystem, seed banks preserve genetic strains for long periods, and sacred

128224.subject: Zoology
128224.text: Tadpoles can be made to grow in size and become adult by
options: feeding the eggs of other frogs
providing them with suitable climatic conditions.
128224.sol: Tadpoles can be made to grow in size and become adult by injecting thyroxine hormone. The process by which tadpole grows in size and becomes adult is known as metamorphosis. The amphibian metamorphosis is under neuroendocrine control.

128918.subject: Zoology
128918.text: What is the innermost layer of an artery and vein?
128918.sol: The blood flows strictly by a fixed route through Blood Vessels—the arteries and veins. Basically, each artery and vein consists of three layers: an inner lining of squamous endothelium, the tunica intima , a middle layer of smooth muscle and elastic fibres, the tunica media, and an external layer of fibrous connective tissue with collagen fibres, the tunica externa. The tunica media is comparatively thin in the veins

129410.subject: Zoology
options: In amniotes last nerve is spinal accessory.
In non-amniotes last nerve is vagus.
129410.sol: 10 pairs of cranial nerves are present in anamniotes (fishes and amphibians) and 12 pairs occur in amniotes (reptiles, birds and mammals). In anamniotes the cranial nerves are - Olfactory, Optic, Occulomotor, Trochlear, Trigeminal, Abducens, Facial, Auditory, Glossopharyngeal and Vagus. In amniotes two more cranial nerves, Spinal accessory and Hypoglossal nerves are present in addition to the above ten.

129546.subject: Zoology
129546.text: What hormone regulates the water reabsorption in the kidneys?
129546.sol: Osmoreceptors in the body are activated by changes in blood volume, body fluid volume and ionic concentration. An excessive loss of fluid from the body can activate these receptors which stimulate the hypothalamus to release antidiuretic hormone (ADH) or vasopressin from the neurohypophysis. ADH facilitates water reabsorption from latter parts of the tubule, thereby preventing diuresis . An increase in body fluid volume can switch off the osmoreceptors and suppress the ADH release to complete the feedback. ADH can

129687.subject: Zoology
129687.text: A person experiences a significant increase in body fluid volume and blood pressure, leading to increased blood flow to the atria of the heart. Which of the following regulatory responses will be initiated to maintain homeostasis?
options: Release of Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF) from the atrial wall
Activation of juxtaglomerular (JG) cells to release renin
Secretion of aldosterone from the adrenal cortex
Release of antidiuretic hormone (ADH) from the neurohypophysis
129687.sol: An increase in blood flow to the atria of the heart triggers the release of Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF) from the atrial wall. ANF causes vasodilation and decreases blood pressure, acting as a check on the renin-angiotensin mechanism. High blood volume and elevated blood pressure suppress the release of renin from JG cells, aldosterone from the adrenal cortex, and ADH from the neurohypophysis, as these hormones function to increase blood volume and pressure. Answer: Release of Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF) fro

130087.subject: Zoology
130087.text: In the sequence of respiration in humans, which physiological step acts as the chronological link between the exchange of gases occurring across the simple squamous epithelium of the alveoli and the exchange of gases occurring at the systemic capillaries?
options: Diffusion of O ₂ and CO ₂ between blood and tissues
Transport of gases by the blood
130087.sol: Respiration in humans occurs in a specific sequence of five steps. The exchange of gases across the simple squamous epithelium of the alveoli represents the second step (alveolar diffusion). The exchange of gases at the systemic capillaries represents the fourth step (diffusion of O ₂ and CO ₂ between blood and tissues). The physiological step that chronologically and functionally links these two events is the third step, which is the transport of gases by the blood. Pulmonary ventilation is the first step (occurri

130245.subject: Zoology
130245.text: Where is the vertebral column located in the human body?
130245.sol: The Skeletal system is grouped into two main divisions - the axial skeleton which includes the bones that make up the central axis of the body such as the skull, spinal column, rib cage and the appendicular skeleton which includes bones of the upper and lower limbs and the bones that attach the limbs to the axial skeleton. Bones play a crucial role in supporting and providing structure to the human body. They also protect delicate organs, store minerals, and produce blood cells.The human body consists of 206 bones

130294.subject: Zoology
options: Inflammation of joints due to accumulation of uric acid crystals
Progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle mostly due to genetic disorder
Auto immune disorder affecting neuromuscular junction leading to fatigue, weakening and paralysis of skeletal
Rapid spasms (wild contractions) in muscle due to low Ca²⁺ in body fluid
130294.sol: .The human body consists of 206 bones in total. These bones are grouped into two main divisions - the axial skeleton and the appendicular skeleton. The skull is composed of two sets of bones, cranial and facial, that total to 22 bones.Each vertebra has a central hollow portion (neural canal) through which the spinal cord passes. The vertebral column is differentiated into cervical (7), thoracic (12), lumbar (5), sacral (1-fused) and coccygeal (1-fused) regions..The flat skull bones fuse end-to-end with the help of

130466.subject: Zoology
130466.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): The vertebral column of an adult human consists of 26 serially arranged units called vertebrae. Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
130466.sol: Assertion (A) is true because the adult human vertebral column is formed by 26 serially arranged units. Reason (R) is also true and correctly explains the Assertion. 130561.text: What principle do natural methods of contraception work on?
options: Avoiding chances of ovum and sperm meeting
130561.sol: Natural methods work on the principle of avoiding chances of ovum and sperms meeting. Periodic abstinence is one such method in which the couples avoid or abstain from coitus from day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle when ovulation could be expected. As chances of fertilisation are very high during this period, it is called the fertile period. Therefore, by abstaining from coitus during this period, conception could be prevented. These enzymes are highly efficient enzymes as they have to catalyze polymerisation of a large number of nucleotides in a very short time. 131831.text: Match the genes of the lac operon in List-I with their respective protein products in List-II. List-I List-II (A) i gene (I) Transacetylase (B) z gene (II) Permease (C) y gene (III) -galactosidase (D) a gene (IV) Repressor protein Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
131831.sol: The lac operon consists of one regulatory gene and three structural genes. The i gene codes for the repressor protein of the lac operon. The z gene codes for -galactosidase, which is primarily responsible for the hydrolysis of lactose into galactose and glucose. The y gene codes for permease, which increases the permeability of the cell to -galactosides. The a gene codes for a transacetylase. Therefore, the correct match is (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I). Answer: (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)

95858.sol: Protozoa include all single-celled, eukaryotic organisms without a cell wall and they also show the heterotrophic mode of nutrition, but main reason for classifying these organisms into separate phylum is due to presence of locomotory organelles. 95917.sol: Potato spindle tuber disease affects the potato plant where the tubers are malformed and stunts the growth of the plant. This disease is caused by viroids which are smaller than virus and without any capsid covering of protein. It is basically a free floating single strand RNA.

96116.subject: Botany
96116.text: Intracellular space is divided into two distinct compartments, i.e., luminal and extraluminal in:
96116.sol: The network of tiny tubular structures is scattered in the cytoplasm of the eukaryotic cell. This network is called the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). This ER divides the intracellular space into luminal (inside the reticulum) and extraluminal (in the cytoplasm) compartments. If the reticulum has ribosomes on their surface, they are called rough endoplasmic reticulum and if no ribosomes are present then they are known as the smooth endoplasmic reticulum.

96162.subject: Botany
96162.text: Meiosis-I is also called as heterotypic division/reductional cell division. Select the correct option by comparing the phase of the meiosis and their respective events from lists I and II. List I (Phase of meiosis) List II (Event that occurs) 1. Prophase I Crossing over occurs 2. Metaphase I Sister chromatids migrate to opposite poles 3. Anaphase I Homologous chromosomes line up at equator in pairs
96162.sol: Crossing over is the exchange of genetic material between homologous chromosomes which occurs during prophase I of meiosis during a process called a synopsis. During metaphase, the homologous chromosomes line up at the equator in pairs and in anaphase, the sister chromatids migrate towards opposite poles.

96218.subject: Botany
96218.text: Select incorrect statements. 1 . Diplotene stage is not recognized by the dissolution of the synaptonemal complex. 2 . Recombination nodules contain a recombinase enzyme. 3 . Interkinesis is generally short-lived. 4 . In anaphase II separation of homologous chromosomes (bivalent) separate to opposite poles.
96218.sol: In the diplotene stage, the synaptonemal complex starts dissolution or disintegrating and the chromosomes start separating after crossing over. Recombination nodules contain a recombinase enzyme which helps in the process of recombination. Separation of homologous chromosomes (bivalent) occurs during anaphase I and this is known as disjunction, it results in a reduction in chromosome number to half. In anaphase II chromatids of a chromosome separate to opposite poles with the splitting the centromere taking place.

97559.subject: Botany
options: The algal cell wall is made up of cellulose, algin, pectin and polysulphate esters.
Most of the gymnosperms are homosporous.
Most of the pteridophytes are heterosporous, and some are homosporous.
Water is not required for fertilisation in seed plants like Selaginella and Salvinia.
97559.sol: In Chlorophyceae, the cell wall is made up of cellulose. In Rhodophyceae, the cell wall is made up of cellulose, pectin and polysulphate esters. In Phaeophyceae, the cell wall is made up of cellulose and algin. Gymnosperms are heterosporous, and most of the Pteridophytes are homosporous, and some are heterosporous like Selaginella and Salvinia. Both these plants produce two kinds of spores, macro (large) and micro (small) spores showing a tendency towards seed formation.

97701.subject: Botany
97701.text: Which of the following is the intermediate compound linking glycolysis to the Krebs' cycle?
97701.sol: During glycolysis pyruvic acid is produced from glucose and is oxidatively decarboxylated to form acetyl C o A . The oxidation of pyruvic acid occurs inside matrix of mitochondria and is called as link reaction. It results in production of 2 molecules of C O 2 and 2 molecules of N A D H 2 . This acetyl C o A is completely oxidised during Krebs' cycle. Thus acetyl C o A acts as the linker of glycolysis and Krebs' cycle.

6a7a1ff8767a8d816fe9ecbc.text: An aromatic primary amide A undergoes Hoffmann bromamide degradation to give an amine B . B is treated with NaNO₂ and HCl at 0-5^ C to form C . C is reacted with CuCN/KCN to form D . Complete acidic hydrolysis of D yields an aromatic carboxylic acid E which has a molar mass of 122 g mol ⁻¹ . The molar mass of the starting amide A is _______ g mol ⁻¹ .
6a7a1ff8767a8d816fe9ecbc.sol: The aromatic carboxylic acid E has a molar mass of 122 g mol ⁻¹ . This corresponds to benzoic acid, C₆H₅COOH ( 72 + 5 + 12 + 32 + 1 = 122 g mol ⁻¹ ). Tracing the reaction sequence backwards: Complete acidic hydrolysis of a nitrile ( D ) yields a carboxylic acid. Thus, D is benzonitrile, C₆H₅CN . Reaction of a diazonium salt ( C ) with CuCN/KCN yields a nitrile. Thus, C is benzenediazonium chloride, C₆H₅N₂^+Cl^- . Diazotization of a primary aromatic amine ( B ) yields a diazonium salt. Thus, B is aniline, C₆H₅NH₂ .

6a7a1ff8650884928d0bf11a.text: Match List I with List II. List I (Biopolymer) List II (Characteristic Linkage) A. Amylose I. Peptide linkage B. Cellulose II. Phosphodiester linkage C. Protein III. -Glycosidic linkage D. Nucleic acid IV. -Glycosidic linkage Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
6a7a1ff8650884928d0bf11a.sol: Amylose is a linear polymer of -D-glucose units connected by -glycosidic linkages. Cellulose is a straight chain polysaccharide composed only of -D-glucose units which are joined by -glycosidic linkages. Proteins are polymers of -amino acids connected by peptide linkages. Nucleic acids (DNA and RNA) are long chain polymers of nucleotides, which are linked by phosphodiester linkages. Therefore, the correct matching is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II. Answer: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

6a7a1ff8b8a1e58543e32bf1.text: When an aqueous solution of D-fructose is treated with a dilute alkali and allowed to stand for some time, it undergoes the Lobry de Bruyn-van Ekenstein rearrangement. Which of the following represents the major monosaccharide components present in the resulting equilibrium mixture?
6a7a1ff8b8a1e58543e32bf1.sol: In the presence of a dilute alkali, D-fructose undergoes deprotonation at the -carbon to form a planar enediol intermediate. When this enediol intermediate undergoes reprotonation to form an aldose, the proton can add from either face of the double bond. This results in the formation of two C-2 epimers: D-glucose and D-mannose. Since the reaction is reversible, the final equilibrium mixture contains the unreacted D-fructose along with D-glucose and D-mannose. Answer: D-fructose, D-glucose and D-mannose
